paragraphs: A fabric gazebo is a roof that admits it is temporary. The frame folds, the canopy is replaceable, and the whole structure is designed around one weekend at a time rather than around a planning application.
The model holds 157,578 polygons and 80,354 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $31 it suits garden and exterior visualisation, event and hospitality scenes, e-commerce and retail imagery, architectural renders, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2023.

A stiff sole is what separates a hiking boot from a shoe that looks like one. The rigidity is deliberate: it lets the edge of the boot take weight on a rock, and it is the reason walking on pavement in them is so unpleasant.

The model holds 95,454 polygons and 98,820 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 8192x8192, which is unusually generous for footwear. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $31 it suits footwear and outdoor visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, character accessories, advertising, film costume and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

White chocolate contains no cocoa solids at all, which is why purists argue it is not chocolate. It is cocoa butter, sugar and milk, and the tempering is harder than for dark because there is nothing in it to hide a mistake.
The model is supplied in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.
At $31 it suits food and confectionery visualisation, packaging and menu imagery, advertising, kitchen and production scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A plinth is the most underestimated object in exhibition design. It sets the viewing height, defines how close anybody can stand, and decides whether what is on top reads as an artefact or as a thing somebody left there.
This is supplied as a base prepared for printing, and it is built to CheckMate specification.
At $31 it suits museum and exhibition work, product and display presentation, collectible and figure basing, retail scenes, printable model production and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A straddle stacker keeps its legs on the floor either side of the load instead of carrying a counterweight, which makes it far lighter and far narrower. It cannot lift off a lorry bed, and inside a stockroom that does not matter at all.

The model is light at 56,098 polygons and 30,407 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged so the mast and forks can be posed or animated. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $31 it suits warehouse and logistics visualisation, equipment marketing, training and safety material, retail stockrooms, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.

The can beat the bottle on every measurable count and lost on none except sentiment. It chills faster, blocks light completely, weighs less to ship and stacks, and craft brewers who resisted it for years now put their best beer in one.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the cans as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $30 the set suits packaging and label mockups, beverage and product visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, bar scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Massage slippers are a product built on a premise the wearer either believes or does not. The nodules are placed according to reflexology maps, and the entire user experience is a few weeks of discomfort followed by either habit or a bin.
The model holds 108,720 polygons and 63,732 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in pink. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits product and wellness visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, interior and bathroom scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The trolley in an airport terminal is deliberately hard to steer and impossible to take outside. Both are design decisions: one keeps it slow near crowds, the other keeps the fleet inside the building where it can be collected.
The model is light at 43,388 polygons and 22,096 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits airport and terminal visualisation, transport and hospitality scenes, equipment marketing, film sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

The alpine butterfly makes a loop in the middle of a rope that can be pulled in any direction without slipping, and it unties after being loaded, which almost no other knot manages. Climbers use it for exactly that combination.

The model is extremely light at 1,160 polygons and 1,178 vertices, built at subdivision level with non-overlapping UVs, so it smooths cleanly at any scale. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits climbing and outdoor education, technical illustration, equipment marketing, instructional material, game props and editorial work. On sale since 2021.

The cheap tablet found its market by being disposable. It is bought for children, kitchens and long flights, and the calculation is explicitly that losing one should not matter, which is a specification no premium device can meet.
The model carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits product and technology visualisation, screen and interface mockups, e-commerce imagery, interior and desk scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.
An e reader is the rare device that succeeds by doing less. No notifications, no colour, a screen that does nothing when the page is still, and a battery measured in weeks because of it.
The model is extremely light at 2,207 polygons and 2,338 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification.
At $29 it suits product and technology visualisation, screen mockups, e-commerce imagery, reading and interior scenes, advertising, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

The steel ammunition box is one of the most reused objects in the world. It is watertight, stackable and almost impossible to destroy, which is why so many end up holding tools, tackle and everything else long after the contents were fired.
The model is light at 22,947 polygons and 23,085 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits defence visualisation, film and television set dressing, game environments, documentary graphics, workshop scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

The charger is the accessory everybody loses and nobody chooses. It is designed to be forgettable, which is a genuinely difficult brief, and the only visible decisions are the size of the block and how the cable leaves it.
The model is very light at 8,798 polygons and 9,004 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits product and technology visualisation, e-commerce and packaging imagery, advertising, desk and interior scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The tall white router was a deliberate refusal of the category. Everything else on the market was black, flat and covered in antennas; this one stood upright and hid them, and it was discontinued while still being the best looking device of its kind.

The model is light at 15,416 polygons and 15,408 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps, 5 at 3072x3072 and one at 512x512. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits product and design visualisation, e-commerce imagery, office and interior scenes, period technology presentation, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.
